| stand_still | -0.3 | (Σ_all abs(δq)-4)*S. At the default standing pose f=-4, giving a positive reward of 1.2*dt. The subtraction is left unclamped. |
| volume_points_penetration | -4 | Sum of penetration_depth(point)*(norm(v_point)+1e-6) over 100 points on each foot. See Sections 10.2.7 and 10.3. |
| feet_air_time | 0.5 | min(left_mode_time,right_mode_time)*M during single support. Mode time is current_contact_time in contact and current_air_time otherwise. Double support and flight give zero. |
| feet_slide | -0.4 | Sum of norm(foot COM world linear velocity_xy)*C_i over the feet. |
| joint_deviation_hip | -0.5 | Sum of δq² over the four hip_yaw and hip_roll joints. hip_pitch is excluded. |
| ang_vel_xy_l2 | -0.05 | ωx²+ωy² |
| dof_torques_l2 | -1.5e-7 | Sum of τ_actual² over 12 leg joints, using applied torque from qfrc_actuator. |
| dof_acc_l2 | -1.25e-7 | Sum of qacc_actual² over all 29 joints. |
| dof_vel_l2 | -1e-4 | Sum of dq² over all 29 joints. |
| action_rate_l2 | -0.005 | Σ(a-a_prev)² |
| flat_orientation_l2 | -3 | gT_x²+gT_y² |
| pelvis_orientation_l2 | -3 | gP_x²+gP_y² |
| feet_flat_ori | -0.4 | Sum of norm(gF_xy)*C_i over the feet. The L2 norm is unsquared. |
| feet_at_plane | -0.1 | Sum over feet of C_i times the sum of clamp(z_foot_link-z_hit-0.035,0,0.3) over the two downward rays per foot. Infinite hits use the source's zero replacement. |
| feet_close_xy | 0.4 | exp(-max(0,0.12-distance_y)/0.05)-1, where distance_y is the absolute lateral separation in the torso heading frame. This term is nonpositive, so its positive weight penalizes feet that are too close. |
| energy | -5e-5 | Sum of (τ_actual*dq/kp)² over the 12 leg joints. The source uses this stiffness-scaled squared quantity in place of the common sum(abs(tau*dq)). |
| freeze_upper_body | -0.004 | Sum of abs(δq) over 17 waist, shoulder, elbow and wrist joints. |
| dof_pos_limits | -1 | Σ(max(q_soft_lo-q,0)+max(q-q_soft_hi,0)), where the soft range uses a factor of 0.9 on the original joint range. |
| dof_vel_limits | -1 | Σ clamp(abs(dq)-0.9*velocity_limit,0,1) |
| torque_limits | -0.01 | Sum of max(abs(τ_actual)-0.8*effort_limit,0)² over all 29 joints. |
| undesired_contacts | -1 | Sum of 1[Fmax>1N] over all robot bodies minus the same sum over the two ankle_roll bodies. Only those two bodies are excluded. Their parent or child subtrees remain eligible. |

Foot position is the link origin, whereas foot linear velocity is evaluated at the COM: v_COM = v_link + ω × (R * body_ipos). The torso follows the same convention, also adding the runtime COM offset from the context. See `src/wmac_perceptive/hiking_rewards.py:49-55`.

The 13 supervised reward auxiliaries in `hiking_rewards.py:38-44,61-79` are, in order: summed squared leg torques, summed squared accelerations of all joints, leg energy cost, torque-limit excess, non-foot contact count, maximum torso net contact force, maximum left and right foot net contact forces, ungated single-stance time, left/right current_air_time and left/right current_contact_time. Contact `history_length=3` retains the last three physical force updates at the end of a control step. Physics decimation is 4. `HikingContactSensor` tests the >1 N predicate and accumulates elapsed air/contact time on each physics substep (`hiking_rewards.py:160-181`). It does not add a fixed 0.02 s once per control step.

### 10.2 Interpretation and gradients of individual rewards


The formulas use ASCII so they can be pasted into a plain code block in Feishu without a LaTeX renderer.

```text
physics_dt = 0.005
decimation = 4
control_dt = physics_dt * decimation = 0.02
raw_task = sum(weight[name] * raw_term[name] for name in 26_rewards)
task_reward = control_dt * raw_task
style_reward = 0.25 * max(0, 1 - 0.25 * (D(amp_history) - 1)^2)
total_reward = task_reward + style_reward
```

The signs of the weights already account for reward and penalty direction. The standing term and foot-separation term can both take negative raw values, so the weight alone does not determine the behavior.

Here, “has a gradient” refers to gradients with respect to continuous world-model outputs during actor imagination. Physical data collection does not backpropagate through MuJoCo.

#### 10.2.1 Linear velocity tracking (`track_lin_vel_xy_exp`, weight 2)

```text
f = exp(-sum((command_xy - torso_COM_velocity_body_xy)^2) / 0.25)
contribution = 0.02 * 2 * f
```

This encourages the robot to reach the commanded planar velocity in the torso frame, with a maximum contribution of 0.04 per step.
Gradients flow through both velocity and the continuous command generated by target navigation. Discrete target selection happens during physical collection and is outside the gradient path.
Large velocity errors drive the exponential and its gradient toward zero. Other task terms, initial state sampling and AMP also help the policy discover feasible behavior.

#### 10.2.2 Angular velocity tracking (`track_ang_vel_z_exp`, weight 2)

```text
f = exp(-(command_yaw_rate - torso_body_omega_z)^2 / 0.25)
contribution = 0.02 * 2 * f
```

This encourages left and right yaw turns, with a maximum contribution of 0.04 per step.
Gradients flow through angular velocity and the continuous command. The exponential gradient again decays for very large errors.

#### 10.2.3 Turn command cost (`heading_error`, weight -1)

```text
f = abs(command_yaw_rate)
contribution = -0.02 * f
```

The source penalizes commanded yaw rate to encourage the robot to face its target more directly.
The term measures navigation controller output. Torso-to-target heading error affects the reward through this controller, and command clipping cuts off that gradient path at saturation.
PyTorch uses a subgradient of the absolute value at zero. This function is not globally smooth.

#### 10.2.4 Failure to advance (`dont_wait`, weight -0.5)

```text
f = indicator(command_x > 0.3) * (
    indicator(velocity_x < 0.15)
  + indicator(velocity_x < 0)
  + indicator(velocity_x < -0.15))
contribution = -0.01 * f
```

When the command clearly requests forward motion, this progressively penalizes stalling and increasingly fast backward movement.
Imagination retains the three Boolean comparisons in the original formula. They have no direct continuous gradient almost everywhere. They still affect numerical returns, critic targets and other paths through future rewards. Substituting a sigmoid would change this term.

#### 10.2.5 Survival (`is_alive`, weight 3)

```text
f_real = 1 - hard_terminated
f_imagined_v3 = 1 - predicted_soft_death_probability
contribution = 0.06 * f
```

This discourages falls and impacts on the torso.
The physical threshold gives a Boolean result. Imagined termination uses a continuous probability with consistent forward and backward values. It sends gradients to the actor through both this immediate term and the survival product weighting future returns.

#### 10.2.6 Standing posture (`stand_still`, weight -0.3)

```text
standing = (norm(command_xy) < 0.15) and (abs(command_yaw_rate) < 0.15)
f = (sum(abs(joint_pos - default_joint_pos)) - 4) * standing
contribution = -0.006 * f
```

This maintains the default standing pose at low command speeds. At that pose f=-4 and the per-step contribution is +0.024.
The standing gate is nondifferentiable. When it is open, the L1 distance of joint offsets has a subgradient. A ReLU after subtracting 4 would change the task.

#### 10.2.7 Foot penetration at edges (`volume_points_penetration`, weight -4)

```text
penetration(point) = max_over_valid_edge_cylinders(max(0, radius - radial_distance))
f = sum_over_200_foot_points(penetration(point) * (norm(point_velocity) + 1e-6))
contribution = -0.08 * f
```

This discourages fast penetration by the foot volume near sharp stair or obstacle edges, reducing the risk of stepping on an edge.
Inside a selected cylinder, point position and velocity have piecewise gradients. Candidate indices, axial inclusion and switches between maxima are discrete or nondifferentiable. Outside all cylinders the term and its gradient are zero.
This geometric reward uses known, static terrain. The WM learns contact dynamics. The term itself does not simulate full differentiable foot-ground contact.

#### 10.2.8 Single-support time (`feet_air_time`, weight 0.5)

```text
mode_time[i] = contact_time[i] if contact_time[i] > 0 else air_time[i]
f = min(mode_time[left], mode_time[right]) if exactly_one_foot_in_contact else 0
f = f * moving_command
contribution = 0.01 * f
```

With a motion command, this encourages alternating single support and discourages keeping both feet planted for long periods. Longer flight alone does not increase the reward.
Auxiliary dimension 8 is directly supervised with the observed ungated value. Its imagined prediction supplies gradients, while the Boolean command gate remains nondifferentiable.

#### 10.2.9 Foot sliding (`feet_slide`, weight -0.4)

```text
f = sum_over_feet(norm(foot_COM_world_velocity_xy) * contact_indicator)
contribution = -0.008 * f
```

This discourages horizontal sliding of a foot in contact with the ground.
Gradients flow to foot velocity. The `contact_indicator` compares predicted foot force to 1 N, so that path has no direct derivative with respect to force. Contact-dependent terms do not all differentiate directly through contact force.

#### 10.2.10 Hip deviation (`joint_deviation_hip`, weight -0.5)

```text
f = sum_over_hip_yaw_and_hip_roll((joint_pos - default_joint_pos)^2)
contribution = -0.01 * f
```

This constrains the four hip yaw/roll joints to discourage excessive toe-in, toe-out and lateral lean. The set excludes hip pitch.
This smooth quadratic joint term backpropagates directly through the GenCoord state, WM and actor.

#### 10.2.11 Torso roll and pitch rates (`ang_vel_xy_l2`, weight -0.05)

```text
f = torso_body_omega_x^2 + torso_body_omega_y^2
contribution = -0.001 * f
```

This suppresses torso roll/pitch oscillation while leaving the desired yaw rate unpenalized by this term.
The continuous angular velocity receives the usual gradient of a quadratic.

#### 10.2.12 Leg torques (`dof_torques_l2`, weight -1.5e-7)

```text
f = sum_over_12_leg_joints(actual_applied_torque^2)
contribution = -0.02 * 1.5e-7 * f
```

This reduces lower-limb actuator load. The physical torque after saturation comes from `qfrc_actuator`.
Imagination uses dimension 0 of the 13-dimensional auxiliary prediction. The actor receives gradients through the head's dependence on state and action. The physical MuJoCo torque calculation is outside that path.

#### 10.2.13 Joint accelerations (`dof_acc_l2`, weight -1.25e-7)

```text
f = sum_over_29_joints(actual_joint_acceleration^2)
contribution = -0.02 * 1.25e-7 * f
```

This discourages high-acceleration impacts and promotes smoother motion.
The supervision target is physical `qacc`. The imagined reward uses auxiliary dimension 1. The control-step difference `(dq_next-dq)/control_dt` would represent a different quantity from the actual substep acceleration.

#### 10.2.14 Joint velocities (`dof_vel_l2`, weight -1e-4)

```text
f = sum_over_29_joints(joint_velocity^2)
contribution = -0.000002 * f
```

This reduces unnecessary high-speed joint motion.
The term reads dq directly from the GenCoord successor state and has a continuous gradient. The noisy, scaled dq supplied to the proprioceptive observations is unsuitable here.

#### 10.2.15 Change in action (`action_rate_l2`, weight -0.005)

```text
f = sum((current_action - previous_action)^2)
contribution = -0.0001 * f
```

This suppresses jitter in successive commands.
During imagination, `previous_action` is the previous imagined action. It stays attached to the graph, so this quadratic sends gradients to both adjacent actions. At the start of the rollout, `previous_action` is a constant from physical replay.

#### 10.2.16 Torso orientation (`flat_orientation_l2`, weight -3)

```text
f = torso_projected_gravity_x^2 + torso_projected_gravity_y^2
contribution = -0.06 * f
```

This encourages a vertical torso.
Gradients pass continuously through the quaternion and FK. Both exactly upright and exactly inverted orientations have zero projected gravity in xy. Other terms, including termination and AMP, constrain the inverted pose.

#### 10.2.17 Pelvis orientation (`pelvis_orientation_l2`, weight -3)

```text
f = pelvis_projected_gravity_x^2 + pelvis_projected_gravity_y^2
contribution = -0.06 * f
```

Keeping the pelvis vertical complements the torso orientation term and discourages excessive waist bending to compensate for torso tilt.
The gradient flows through the pelvis quaternion. Reusing torso gravity here would discard the independent pelvis constraint.

#### 10.2.18 Stance foot orientation (`feet_flat_ori`, weight -0.4)

```text
f = sum_over_feet(norm(foot_projected_gravity_xy) * contact_indicator)
contribution = -0.008 * f
```

This encourages a foot in contact to stay approximately level.
The continuous part uses the unsquared norm. The foot quaternion receives a subgradient. The Boolean contact gate has no direct gradient.

#### 10.2.19 Stance foot height above the support plane (`feet_at_plane`, weight -0.1)

```text
height_error[i,ray] = clamp(foot_link_z[i] - ray_hit_z[i,ray] - 0.035, 0, 0.3)
f = sum_over_feet(contact_indicator[i] * sum_over_two_rays(height_error[i,ray]))
contribution = -0.002 * f
```

During contact, the foot-link pose should agree with the thickness of the sole and the height of the nearby support surface.
Distance inside the selected terrain triangle has a piecewise gradient. The gradient is zero outside the clamp. Box-hit boundaries and discrete choices of ray hit are nondifferentiable. Infinite ray values follow the source's zero-replacement rule.

#### 10.2.20 Lateral foot separation (`feet_close_xy`, weight +0.4)

```text
distance_y = abs(-sin(torso_heading) * feet_difference_x
                  + cos(torso_heading) * feet_difference_y)
f = exp(-max(0, 0.12 - distance_y) / 0.05) - 1
contribution = 0.008 * f
```

Lateral foot separation below 0.12 m incurs a penalty, discouraging crossed legs or an excessively narrow base of support. Increasing the stance width beyond the threshold earns no further reward.
Inside the threshold there is a continuous gradient. Beyond it the ReLU and gradient are zero. At zero, absolute value uses a subgradient.

#### 10.2.21 Energy proxy (`energy`, weight -5e-5)

```text
f = sum_over_12_leg_joints((actual_torque * actual_joint_velocity / actual_kp)^2)
contribution = -0.000001 * f
```

The source defines a power proxy divided by stiffness and then squared. Replacing this with conventional mechanical work or absolute power would change the objective.
Auxiliary dimension 2 predicts it in imagination. The physical target retains the actual τ, dq and kp. Training in log1p space controls the dynamic range.

#### 10.2.22 Upper body posture (`freeze_upper_body`, weight -0.004)

```text
f = sum_over_17_waist_shoulder_elbow_wrist_joints(abs(joint_pos - default_joint_pos))
contribution = -0.00008 * f
```

This discourages unnecessary upper-body motion while allowing benefits from other task and balance rewards to offset the cost.
The term measures L1 position error and uses a subgradient at zero deviation. It does not measure squared upper-body speed.

#### 10.2.23 Soft joint position limits (`dof_pos_limits`, weight -1)

```text
f = sum(max(soft_joint_lower - joint_pos,0)
      + max(joint_pos - soft_joint_upper,0))
contribution = -0.02 * f
```

These limits provide a 10% margin before the hard physical limits.
Within the soft range both cost and gradient are zero. Outside it the penalty increases linearly. Read the position limits from the specific MJCF rather than inferring the mapping from 29 joint indices.

#### 10.2.24 Soft joint velocity limits (`dof_vel_limits`, weight -1)

```text
f = sum(clamp(abs(joint_velocity) - 0.9 * source_velocity_limit, 0, 1))
contribution = -0.02 * f
```

This penalizes excessive speed relative to the motor thresholds in the source configuration, with a maximum of 1 per joint.
There is a gradient above the soft threshold until the clamp saturates, after which the gradient is zero. MuJoCo does not impose this source `velocity_limit` as a hard limit equivalent to the PhysX solver's limit.

#### 10.2.25 Soft torque limits (`torque_limits`, weight -0.01)

```text
f = sum_over_29_joints(max(abs(actual_torque) - 0.8 * effort_limit, 0)^2)
contribution = -0.0002 * f
```

This imposes an additional cost on actuator load near rated effort across all joints. The separate τ² penalty applies only to the legs.
The physical term uses saturated torque τ. Imagination uses auxiliary dimension 3. An unsaturated PD formula would give a different label.

#### 10.2.26 Non-foot contacts (`undesired_contacts`, weight -1)

```text
f = count(all_robot_body_max_force > 1N) - count(two_ankle_roll_body_max_force > 1N)
contribution = -0.02 * f
```

This discourages ground contacts by the knees, hands, torso and other non-foot bodies.
The physical count is an integer. Auxiliary dimension 4 predicts a nonnegative continuous count and permits gradients through the WM inputs. Rounding the prediction before differentiating would break this path.

### 10.3 Full geometry for foot interactions with edges

Full Hiking uses the unshod G1 foot volume. Each foot has 10 × 5 × 2 = 100 points spanning x from -0.025 to 0.12, y from -0.03 to 0.03 and z from -0.04 to 0, including endpoints (`src/wmac_perceptive/safety.py:30-64`). Transform these points to world coordinates first. The upstream point-velocity formula is foot COM world linear velocity + ω × (point - link_origin). This differs from the strict rigid-body point-velocity formula but reproduces the authors' implementation.

Extract sharp edges with adjacent-face angles >70° from the actual MuJoCo heightfield triangles and yaw-rotated box meshes. Greedily merge edges with a 30° continuation criterion and a 0.05 m fit tolerance. Each edge defines a finite, flat-ended cylinder of radius 0.05 m. The point's axial projection must lie in [0,length]. Among the eligible cylinders, penetration depth is max(max(0,0.05-radial_distance)). The ends are flat, without capsule hemispheres. A spatial hash filters candidates while preserving this formula (`src/tasks/amp_perceptive/hiking_geometry.py:20-101`). Full Hiking adds no height sigmoid or distance-field proxy. The legacy 18-point proxy belongs to a different protocol.

The nominal origins of the two plane rays on each foot are (-0.02,0,20) and (0.10,0,20). Rotate them by foot yaw only, add the foot-link position, and cast vertically down. Use intersections with the **actual MuJoCo triangles and boxes**. Bilinear height raster interpolation gives different results (`src/wmac_perceptive/hiking_rewards.py:31-41`). This geometry is piecewise differentiable. The selected triangle or edge has continuous distance derivatives, while discrete candidates, inside tests, contact gates and changes in the maximum lack smooth derivatives. The complete reward is therefore not smooth everywhere.

### 10.4 Training termination, timeouts and imagined survival

A training episode lasts 20 s, or 1,000 control steps. Physical failure occurs when the maximum net torso contact force over three physics samples exceeds 1 N, tilt exceeds 1 rad, or torso_z-min(env_origin_z,0)<0.5 m. The expression uses zero for a positive origin height and subtracts a negative origin height as upstream does. It does not measure height above the ground directly below the feet. A `terrain_boundary` event or time limit is marked as a timeout, separately from physical failure. The terrain boundary is the rectangular extent of the entire map. Leaving an individual 8 m tile does not trigger it.

Version 3 imagined termination uses the sigmoid applied to the worst normalized criterion from Section 9.1. Take the maximum of the normalized height, tilt and force criteria and apply sigmoid((u-1)/.05) once. Both is_alive and continuation equal 1-p. Survival is the cumulative product. Forward values and derivatives are consistent. Only the maximum criterion contributes to the gate gradient, with subgradients at ties. The probabilistic OR of three sigmoids belongs to v2. The hard+(soft-soft.detach()) estimator belongs to v1.

The hard failures in this section apply to training. The v3 interactive PLAY protocol and standard quantitative evaluation follow upstream PLAY in removing the low-height failure and shortening the episode to 10 s. `zero_start` additionally changes initial state and commands. Section 11.5 lists the full conditions. PLAY leaves the imagination function and the actor's saved training protocol unchanged.

### 10.5 Auxiliary supervision and the 129-dimensional context

The GenCoord physical state has 71 dimensions. Contact timers stay outside the free-joint coordinates.
A single network pass predicts 35 velocity increments, 13 physical auxiliaries and 128 visual latent increments, for a total output width of 176.
Softplus keeps the 13 auxiliary predictions nonnegative. The final-layer biases for these channels are initialized at -4. The training loss is SmoothL1(log1p(pred),log1p(true)).
See `LatentPerceptiveWorldModel.__init__/step_with_latent` and `latent_execution.py:190-225`.

```text
output[0:35]     = root_linear_delta3 + root_angular_delta3 + joint_velocity_delta29
output[35:48]    = 13 nonnegative supervised physical quantities, via softplus
output[48:176]   = 128-dimensional visual latent residual
```

The first 100 dimensions in v3 retain the previous layout. The remaining entries are the actual sliding friction values of the new robot's 29 active collision geoms, sorted by canonical geom name.

| Half-open index range | Width | Contents |
|---|---:|---|
| 0:1 | 1 | Mean sliding friction of the foot collision geoms |
| 1:30 | 29 | Encoder bias. The current full task does not randomize this field. |
| 30:33 | 3 | Torso COM offset from default. The current full task does not randomize this field. |
| 33:34 | 1 | Whether the PD delay history has been initialized |
| 34:35 | 1 | Camera sampling clock, zero for the current fixed 50 Hz camera |
| 35:38 | 3 | World position of the environment's terrain origin |
| 38:67 | 29 | Most recently applied action. context_t holds a_(t-1), and advancing to context_(t+1) writes a_t. |
| 67:96 | 29 | Per-joint delays of 0/1/2 substeps, mapped from the five actuator groups |
| 96:100 | 4 | Left/right current_air_time, then left/right current_contact_time |
| 100:129 | 29 | Actual sliding friction of each collision geom |

`hiking_material_geom_names(3)` compiles the current robot and returns 29 names. `hiking_material_geom_names(2)` still returns 33 names for older checkpoints. Pass the version explicitly to avoid accidentally selecting the default of 2.

Materials still use 64 buckets. Sample static and dynamic friction independently in [0.3,1.6], take dynamic=min(static,dynamic), and sample restitution in [0.05,0.5]. MuJoCo applies only the dynamic sliding friction. Static friction and restitution are recorded without inventing a PhysX mapping. Version 3 draws the bucket matrix on the CPU in row-major order and also samples shape assignments on the CPU before transfer to the device. This reproduces IsaacLab's RNG call order. The older implementation sampled the three columns separately on the GPU. Materials remain fixed after startup. PLAY disables this event and uses μ=1.

WM input width is 435 = 68 state features + 29 actions + 129 conditioning values + 81 terrain values + 128 visual values. Critic input width is 281 = 68 + 3 commands + 129 conditioning values + 81 terrain values. The default MoE actor still takes 896 = 768 proprioceptive + 128 visual values. **The older widths of 311/439/315 no longer describe the current layout.**

The v3 WM action input is the executed position-target transform `action*scale+offset`. Running statistics cover only the 68 state features and 29 processed actions. The DR ranges have separate normalization: `(mu-0.95)/0.65` for friction and `lag-1` for delays. Other context entries retain their established meanings. A single RunningNorm does not normalize all 307 physical input dimensions. See `latent_models.py:117-158`, `hiking_context.py:7-16` and `state.py:113-120`. The algorithm chapters derive the gradient and normalization rules.

## 11. Physical assets, task, sensors, data and operating conditions

### 11.1 The unshod robot and its kinematic tree

#### 11.1.1 Pinned sources and byte-level verification

These Hiking v3 assets determine the robot's actual inertia, joints, collisions and the robot geometry visible in the depth image.

| Local file | Pinned upstream file | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| src/assets/robots/unitree_g1/g1_29dof_torsobase_popsicle.urdf | source/instinctlab/instinctlab/assets/resources/unitree_g1/urdf/g1_29dof_torsobase_popsicle.urdf | 5e99d930af64f3f0bfd34235239e288cc380ba62c8b01fcfcf8cc9f0996e7fa4 |
| src/assets/robots/unitree_g1/hiking_head_link.STL | source/instinctlab/instinctlab/assets/resources/unitree_g1/meshes/head_link.STL | d297328b3569fc85074355e76cba6c889d19de5361224bcd3c5b8ce82e13b9b6 |

Both files come from [InstinctLab de6b92f01eb155d51f30e8ed1ea7aecd2eb1f057](https://github.com/project-instinct/InstinctLab/tree/de6b92f01eb155d51f30e8ed1ea7aecd2eb1f057/source/instinctlab/instinctlab/assets/resources/unitree_g1). The pinned local upstream checkout's HEAD and both file hashes were independently checked against the table.

From the root of a project with the full adapted source already restored, this script can retrieve the two assets again. The remaining 34 visual meshes come from the base project. Restoring the full robot directory also requires those meshes.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import urllib.request

base = ('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/project-instinct/InstinctLab/'
        'de6b92f01eb155d51f30e8ed1ea7aecd2eb1f057/'
        'source/instinctlab/instinctlab/assets/resources/unitree_g1/')
assets = (
    ('urdf/g1_29dof_torsobase_popsicle.urdf',
     'src/assets/robots/unitree_g1/g1_29dof_torsobase_popsicle.urdf',
     '5e99d930af64f3f0bfd34235239e288cc380ba62c8b01fcfcf8cc9f0996e7fa4'),
    ('meshes/head_link.STL',
     'src/assets/robots/unitree_g1/hiking_head_link.STL',
     'd297328b3569fc85074355e76cba6c889d19de5361224bcd3c5b8ce82e13b9b6'),
)
for source, destination, expected in assets:
    content = urllib.request.urlopen(base + source, timeout=60).read()
    assert hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest() == expected, source
    target = Path(destination)
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if target.exists() and target.read_bytes() != content:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Existing asset differs from the pinned version: {target}')
    target.write_bytes(content)
```

This script restores the two pinned assets. Use the self-contained source restoration procedure in this handbook for the full project. Preserve the copyright and license notices referenced in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:103-118`.

#### 11.1.2 Converting URDF physics to the current GenCoord representation

The constructor is `src/tasks/amp_perceptive/hiking_robot.py:get_hiking_robot_spec`. It replaces `g1_constants.get_spec` for this robot.

1. Parse the official torso-base URDF. Temporarily remove the visual nodes to avoid loading visual assets through URDF-relative mesh paths.
2. Add a world and `floating_base_joint` to the source model, with `torso_link` as its free root. Compile through the MuJoCo URDF importer, which merges fixed-link inertia according to its own rules.
3. Read the base project's pelvis-root MJCF as the local kinematic tree. Keep the other 34 visual meshes that match upstream and replace the head mesh contents with the pinned Hiking version.
4. Remove every old MJCF `*_collision` geom and all collision-exclusion pairs.
5. Match bodies by name. Copy mass, COM position, principal inertia-axis quaternion and principal moments, then rebuild the source collision shapes. Convert source cylinders to capsules as prescribed by Hiking's `replace_cylinders_with_capsules=True`.
6. Match joints by name and copy ranges, axes, body offsets and joint centers. Copy branches with the same direction directly. Re-rooting from the torso to the pelvis reverses parent and child for the three waist hinges. Negate their axes and transform the offsets and joint centers inversely so the same named anatomical joint angle q retains its physical meaning.
7. Set the left and right foot marker sites to (0.04,0,-0.037) in each body frame, matching the source LL_FOOT/LR_FOOT coordinates.

**Reversing the waist axes also requires retaining the hinge centers. The child origin is not the pivot for every hinge.** In the local tree, waist_roll has `joint.pos=(0.0039635,0,-0.044)`. FK must retain this pivot. `src/wmac/state.py:133-180` reads axis, pivot and qref from the compiled model and computes poses and twists through hierarchical FK. The older pivot-free simplification gives inconsistent random-waist poses, point velocities and gradients.

This conversion changes the coordinate tree. Do not reverse waist signs a second time in input actions, joint angles or expert data. The 71-dimensional GenCoord state retains the following layout.

```text
state = pelvis_position_world[3], pelvis_quaternion_wxyz[4],
        pelvis_link_linear_velocity_world[3], pelvis_angular_velocity_world[3],
        joint_position[29], joint_velocity[29]
```

Independent CPU compilation produced nbody=31 (including world), njnt=30 (one free and 29 hinges), nq=36, nv=35, ngeom=64 (35 visual and 29 collision), nexclude=0 and total rigid-body mass 33.341142022 kg. The WM uses a 71-dimensional state layout, while MuJoCo splits qpos and qvel into 36 and 35 dimensions respectively. nq alone does not describe the network input.

With random root orientation, joint angles and qvel, `test_hiking_reference_robot.py:43-90` compares each link's pose, COM inertia axes, Jacobian twist and collision shapes across two independently constructed trees. Its nonzero waist samples expose reversed-axis errors that a neutral standing pose can hide. This checks kinematics and asset adaptation. It does not establish identical MuJoCo and PhysX contact dynamics.

#### 11.1.3 Physics settings and contact observations

Version 3 removes the inherited `feet_ground_contact` and `self_collision` sensors. One whole-body `hiking_contact` sensor supplies the contact forces and timers for all rewards and auxiliary labels, alongside `hiking_depth`. The contact sensor still uses net force, history_length=3, track_air_time=True and a 1 N contact predicate. The control period remains 4 × 0.005 s = 0.02 s.

The number of collision shapes with material values drops from 33 to 29, changing the per-geom conditioning schema. Earlier 133-dimensional checkpoints cannot be read as the current 129-dimensional layout. The source robot has no separate shoe collisions. Do not introduce the lowered foot measurement points from `ShoeConfigMixin`.

The full configuration retains `nconmax=256/njmax=700/ccd_iterations=128/contact_sensor_maxmatch=128`. The previously observed minimum of 172 contacts at initialization belongs to an earlier robot/scene combination. The collision geometry changed with the new assets. Measure the actual scene with the capacity probe on the target machine. Body or geom counts alone do not determine the contact pool requirement.

### 11.2 Terrain, commands, resets and actuators

#### 11.2.1 Training environment

Training targets forward walking, left and right turns, in-place turns and rough-terrain walking. Get-ups, running, sidestepping and backward walking lie outside its objectives.
All ten terrain types and fractions are retained: perlin_rough .05, perlin_rough_stand .05, square_gaps .10, pyramid_stairs .15, pyramid_stairs_high .10, pyramid_stairs_inv .15, pyramid_stairs_inv_high .10, boxes .10, mesh_boxes .10 and hf_pyramid_slope_inv .10.
Full training uses a 10 × 20 array of 8 × 8 m tiles with a 3 m border, 0.05 m horizontal resolution, 0.005 m vertical resolution and the full difficulty range. The earlier conservative seven-terrain walking profile is separate.
Walls have probability .3, height 5 m and thickness .05 m. The maximum initial terrain level is 5.
Each tile has 50 flat target patches. Samples taken at multiple radii must have height differences ≤.05 m. Stairs and gaps use the fixed candidate origin+(3.7,0).
The terrain curriculum uses per-episode normalized exponential tracking. Move up when XY>.6 and yaw>0. Move down when XY<.3 and promotion does not apply. Explicit initial resets leave the terrain level unchanged.

The final navigation commands use the same equations.

```text
vx = min(max(2 * target_distance * cos(heading_error), 0), desired_speed)
vy = 0
wz = clip(2 * heading_error, -1, 1)
if distance <= 0.4: navigation_command = 0
```

On ordinary terrain desired_speed is in [.45,.8]. On perlin_rough the upper bound is 1. Standing mode has 5% probability. perlin_rough_stand supplies only a random yaw, sampled in [-1,1] and zeroed for absolute values ≤.5, overriding standing. Resample every 8–12 s. `ranges.lin_vel_x=(0,0)` describes an underlying constant sampling field. The published vx also depends on target navigation.

Version 3 matches the source's RNG call order and command publication timing. It consumes RNG draws for the two constant-zero linear velocity ranges. It samples yaw only for locally reset environments on random-velocity terrain. Resampling writes target, speed and mode first. `_update_command` publishes the final command. The v2 implementation wrote it immediately at the end of `_resample_command`. `commands.py:153-192` and `test_hiking_reference_robot.py:104-133` fix the order of local environments and the expected random results.

Training resets are independent of expert data. Sample torso pose first (z=.9+origin_z, xy and yaw each ±.1), then the six components of torso COM velocity (each ±.2), then q_default±.15 clipped to soft limits. Finally draw joint velocities from their zero-width range. Use the current robot FK to recover the pelvis free-root state. Torso COM velocity must be transformed before writing it at the pelvis. Expert time phase does not determine the physical reset. The formulas in `hiking_resets.py` are unchanged but read the new v3 inertia and geometry.

#### 11.2.2 Five groups of delayed PD actuators

The groups remain legs, feet, waist, waist_yaw and arms. Each environment samples a lag of 0, 1 or 2 physics substeps per group at reset. That lag is fixed throughout the episode.

```text
natural_frequency = 20*pi
kp = effective_armature * natural_frequency^2
kd = 4 * effective_armature * natural_frequency
joint_position_target = default_joint_pos + raw_action * (0.25 * effort_limit / kp)
raw_tau = kp*(delayed_q_target - q) + kd*(delayed_dq_target - dq) + delayed_effort_target
applied_tau = clamp(raw_tau, -effort_limit, effort_limit)
```

| joints | effective armature | effort limit | source velocity soft limit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| hip yaw/pitch, waist yaw | .010177520 | 88 | 32 |
| hip roll, knee | .025101925 | 139 | 20 |
| ankle pitch/roll, waist pitch/roll | 2*.003609725 | 50 | 37 |
| shoulder, elbow, wrist roll | .003609725 | 25 | 37 |
| wrist pitch/yaw | .00425 | 5 | 22 |

The soft position limit factor is .9 and the action scale is given above. Raw policy output is unclipped by default, while actual torque remains bounded. MuJoCo has no hard constraint equivalent to the PhysX joint velocity solver limit. The source velocity thresholds still enter the soft-limit reward. See `hiking_actuators.py:20-60,111-132`.

The default joint pose remains `KNEES_BENT_KEYFRAME` from `g1_constants.py:224-237`. On both sides hip_pitch=-.312, knee=.669, ankle_pitch=-.363, shoulder_pitch=.2 and elbow=.6. Left shoulder_roll=.2 and right shoulder_roll=-.2. The other joints and all default joint velocities are zero. This pose supplies the baseline for δq and the position-action offset. Training adds joint perturbations of ±.15 and solves the torso reset back to the pelvis. A zero_start uses the default pelvis height z=.78 plus the environment origin, default joints and zero velocity.

### 11.3 The fixed, calibrated camera

The current `sensor_protocol=g1_hiking_calibrated_v1` uses measured G1 intrinsics and the fixed nominal Hiking mount. It omits RPL artificial dropout, edge masking, relative Gaussian noise and any translation, rotation or FOV perturbation.

| Parameter | Current value |
|---|---|
| Camera body | torso_link, following full roll/pitch/yaw |
| nominal position | (.0487988662332928,.01,.4378029937970051) m |
| nominal quaternion wxyz | (.9135367613482678,.004363309284746571,.4067366430758002,0) |
| Measured input profile | Depth/Z16, 848 × 480 at 30 Hz |
| Original fx/fy | 431.9433288574219 / 431.9433288574219 |
| Original cx/cy | 432.1478576660156 / 235.75416564941406 |
| 64 × 36 fx/fy | 32.599496517541276 / 32.39574966430664 |
| 64 × 36 cx/cy | 32.15266850309552 / 17.219062423706053 |
| Measured raw depth scale | .0010000000474974513 m/unit |
| Simulated capture | 50 Hz, updated every control step. The measured hardware profile remains 30 Hz. |
| Near range | The raw ray rejects hits at ≤.1 m separately for each geom. |
| Maximum ray range | 2e6 m. Misses and far-end measurements retain 1e6 m. |
| Visible geom groups | (0,2), including physical terrain and robot visual geometry. The parent body is included. |
| Preprocessing | Crop top 18, bottom 0, left 16, right 16 to 18 × 32. Apply a 3 × 3 Gaussian with sigma 1, clip to [0,2.5] and divide by 2.5. |
| History | 37-frame ring, eight frames at stride 5, one-frame delay |

With integer pixel centers, rescale the principal point as `c_new=(c_old+.5)*size_new/size_old-.5`. Scale fx and fy by the horizontal and vertical ratios respectively. Since 64/848 differs from 36/480, the scaled fx and fy differ. The original K gives a boundary FOV of 88.92490338849896° × 58.11279497342982°. The historical 89.51° × 58.29° does not describe the current ray intrinsics.

`ring[-1]` is the current capture. The selected positive indices are (0,5,10,15,20,25,30,35). Their Python negative indices are (-37,-32,-27,-22,-17,-12,-7,-2), corresponding to ages of (36,31,26,21,16,11,6,1) control steps, or (.72,.62,.52,.42,.32,.22,.12,.02) s before the current capture.
The eight frames form an eight-channel input. Raw validity planes are used only for diagnostics and are excluded from the current encoder and decoder.
A missed physical ray retains its 1e6 m value through blurring, then the result is clipped. Prefilling misses with 2.5 m would give them the semantics of artificial dropout.
At termination, sense before capture. Save the reset frame separately and use it to refill the live history. The legacy image-randomization branch must stay disabled in v3.

`g1_hiking_dr_v1` remains available for historical v2 checkpoints and draws on RPL pixel and mounting-error augmentation. Version 3 validation requires the fixed Hiking camera, so an ordinary resume cannot switch to DR. `g1_rpl_depth_v1` is another historical protocol, using 135 × 240 to 27 × 48, 10 Hz, a two-capture delay and centered normalization. The external dual cameras and RPL PPO/distillation training were never imported. A legacy sensor switch does not enable them.

### 11.4 The default expert pool and optional official-only playback

#### 11.4.1 The complete official reference

The official three-file bundle and SHA hashes are unchanged. Its raw NPZ has 18,982 frames at 50 Hz. The authors' exclusive interpolation loads 18,981 frames and retains the full walking timeline, including the original internal concatenations. It applies no per-frame speed, contact or height filtering and no foot-height normalization. Forward differences set the final frame's velocity to zero.

Official AMP features in v3 are computed directly from the source torso positions/quaternions and joint trajectories. Reorder the joints by runtime joint_names. Mirroring swaps left and right, negates roll/yaw joint angles and velocities, and applies the corresponding sagittal reflection to orientation and linear/angular velocity. The policy still uses torso COM velocity, while the official reference takes finite differences of the torso-origin trajectory. This preserves the upstream distinction and avoids reconstructing expert torso velocity through local MuJoCo FK. See `expert.py:175-231`.

#### 11.4.2 The 13 local contiguous segments in the default pool

`walking_expert_source=pre_hiking_local_walk_turn_v2` calls `prepare_locomotion_dataset(...,include_hiking=False,include_grail=False)`. It reads only walking and turning segments from the base project's local WalkandRun files that match the accepted names and the historical local filter.
**The local filter applies only to these supplementary clips. The official Hiking sequence is retained in full.** The default neither downloads GRAIL nor restores Recovery or the locked-pose CSV.

Five source NPZ files supply the 13 original segments. The table gives half-open frame ranges and lengths.

| Source file | [start,end) | Frames |
|---|---|---:|
| arc_walk_left_loop_001__A029.npz | [7,33) | 26 |
| idle_turn_270_001__A048.npz | [131,167) | 36 |
| idle_turn_270_001__A048.npz | [172,196) | 24 |
| walk_arc_cw_loop_002__A046.npz | [229,250) | 21 |
| walk_forward_loop_002__A022.npz | [29,53) | 24 |
| walk_forward_loop_002__A022.npz | [71,117) | 46 |
| walk_forward_loop_002__A022.npz | [154,175) | 21 |
| walk_forward_loop_002__A022.npz | [190,211) | 21 |
| walk_forward_loop_002__A022.npz | [212,234) | 22 |
| walk_forward_loop_002__A022.npz | [255,295) | 40 |
| walk_forward_loop_002__A022.npz | [317,361) | 44 |
| walk_forward_loop_002__A022.npz | [388,417) | 29 |
| walk_forward_loop_002__A024.npz | [431,466) | 35 |

The local clips contain 389 frames. Including mirrors yields 26 clips, 778 frames and 544 valid ten-frame windows. The official original and its mirror contain 37,962 frames and 37,944 windows.
The combined default pool contains 28 clips, 38,740 frames and 38,488 windows. Local windows account for 544/38488 = 1.4134275618374558%. The older standing supplement accounted for 5.9115%.
Sampling is uniform over all valid ten-frame windows, so each clip's effective weight is proportional to its window count. There is no per-clip uniform sampling or command-conditioned pairing. Windows cannot cross original clip, mirror or segment boundaries.

Generated data are written to `cfg.motion_root()/legacy_local_walk_turn_v2`. The immutable manifest checks the file set and SHA hashes of all WalkandRun source files in the base project. Removing a name-filtered file invalidates the old cache even if that file contributed no windows.

#### 11.4.3 Optional official-only episode reference

For a fresh run, `--walking-expert-source none` selects per-environment 50 Hz playback of the official episode reference. On reset, draw a starting fraction in [0,.9] and mirror with 50% probability. Round to the nearest frame and fill the ten-frame history with that first frame. Each physical episode reset selects a new start and mirror. The default mixed pool samples valid windows independently, without this episode clock.

Both v3 options use `standing_expert_source=none`. Zero-speed commands and the `stand_still` task reward still provide a standing objective.

With no arguments, the preparation command now verifies or prepares only the three official raw files.

```bash
python scripts/prepare_mirrored_motions.py
python scripts/audit_wmac_motion_data.py --output /tmp/hiking_raw_audit.json
```

The expert builds the default shared pool at initialization. `--legacy-standing` restores the old walking and locked-pose cache. `--official-walking-only` builds the older FK-converted official cache. Fresh v3 runs need neither cache nor the old four-clip mirror_manifest.

### 11.5 Training, interactive play, quantitative evaluation and zero-start conditions

| Condition | Training (`make_environment(play=False)`) | Interactive (`play_wmac_perceptive`) | Quantitative (`evaluate_wmac_perceptive`) | `zero_start` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Robot | v3 unshod model | Same v3 model recorded in the checkpoint | Same | Same |
| Default environment count | 4,096 | 10, CLI override | 32, CLI override | 32, CLI override |
| Terrain | 10 × 20, 8 m, wall p=.3 | 4 × 10, 8 m, wall p=0 | Inherits PLAY | Default 2 × 2, 12 m, flat heightfield, no walls. training_spawn keeps the PLAY terrain. |
| Episode limit | 20 s | 10 s | 10 s, covered by 500 default steps | max(original PLAY limit, case_duration+1 s) |
| Root height failure | .5 m threshold enabled | Removed | Removed, as in PLAY | Height failure is not automatically reinstated |
| Tilt/torso contact failure | Enabled | Enabled | Enabled | Enabled |
| Terrain curriculum | Enabled | Retained from upstream PLAY | Inherits PLAY | Disabled |
| Proprioceptive observation noise | Enabled | Enabled | Dedicated transform disables all corruption | All corruption disabled |
| Camera pixel/mount DR | Disabled by default | Disabled | Disabled | Disabled |
| Material startup randomization | Enabled | Removed, μ=1 | Same as PLAY, μ=1 | v3 usually inherits PLAY without the event. retained does not re-enable it. |
| Joint reset perturbation | ±.15 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Root pose/twist reset perturbation | xy/yaw ±.1, six twist components ±.2 | Retained | Retained | Independent default pelvis pose, zero qvel, random root ranges disabled |
| PD delay sampling on reset | 0/1/2 per group | Retained | Retained | Retained. nominal does not disable it. |
| Command | Full target/standing/yaw distribution | Upstream PLAY distribution | Same as PLAY | Scripted stand, delayed-start and immediate-start schedules |
| State correction written after action | No | No | No | No. Only the ordinary initial reset is applied. |

See `hiking_task.py:23-91`, `train_wmac_perceptive.py:147-173`, `evaluate_wmac_perceptive.py:201-227` and `evaluate_wmac_zero_start.py:142-188,326-345`.

`g1_amp_perceptive_hiking_env_cfg(play=True)` first sets num_envs=10, then `make_environment` overrides it with cfg.num_envs. This gives interactive play a default of 10 and quantitative evaluation a default of 32, each overridable on the CLI.

Quantitative evaluation has a separate `_quantitative_play_config` that disables observation noise. Interactive PLAY retains it. Quantitative statistics cover the first episode, including its physical terminal transition. Later auto-reset episodes are excluded. Version 3 metadata supersedes the old 0.2–0.7 m/s and depth+valid descriptions. Record actual evaluation conditions from the saved config.

The default zero_start cases are standing for 10 s, waiting 2 s then walking 8 s, and walking immediately for 8 s. The forward command is .5 m/s. `--domain-randomization nominal` removes specified material, encoder, COM and related events while preserving actuator delay. `retained` does not restore all training DR. The initial state uses the local model's default pelvis pose and joint positions with zero qvel. Ordinary training instead samples the torso reset around .9 m.

### 11.6 Contributions of Hiking, InstinctMJ and RPL

Hiking provides the unshod robot, motion reference, task and image conventions. Chapter 6's online reconstruction, latent prediction and stop-gradient implementation follow InstinctMJ. RPL informed earlier camera augmentation experiments. It did not supply the differentiable world model or the camera randomization for the current default.

The legacy `g1_hiking_dr_v1` retains Hiking's 64 × 36 to 18 × 32 preprocessing, 37-frame ring, 50 Hz capture and eight-frame history at stride 5. It adds relative Gaussian noise with std=.1*abs(depth), 5% artificial dropout filled with 2.5 m, ROI edge masking and fixed per-environment mounting errors: XYZ ±.025 m each, Euler ±(2.5,3,2.5) degrees and HFOV ±5 degrees. In the 32-column ROI, small/large masks use left/right widths of (8,3)/(12,7) columns. The base none/small/large probabilities are .1/.45/.45 before terrain bias. The full set of ten terrain names contains no “stepping” name, giving effective probabilities of .1/.3/.6. Physical misses retain 1e6 m until after blurring and clipping, distinct from the artificial dropout fill.

Another legacy protocol, `g1_rpl_depth_v1`, uses 240 × 135 to 48 × 27, 10 Hz capture, a two-capture delay of about 200 ms, clipping to .1..2 m, centered normalization and signed FP16 replay. The external dual camera and RPL PPO/DAgger/distillation system were never imported into this framework.

These settings describe explicit historical protocols. The default v3 `g1_hiking_calibrated_v1` uses measured intrinsics and the fixed nominal Hiking pose without those randomizations. The intrinsics report does not measure the full hardware exposure-to-policy latency or mounting extrinsics. A 30 Hz hardware stream does not generate a fresh image at each simulated 50 Hz control step.

### 12.1 Where to find each implementation

All paths are relative to the restored project root and work independently of the original machine's directory name.

Some module headers describe the mode in use when the module was first introduced. For example, `models.py` describes the pixel model, and `hiking.py` describes the old gate with a hidden layer. Trace calls from `parse_config([])` and the relevant `PerceptiveRunner` branches to identify the active path.

### 12.2 Physical successors, resets, and history windows

A control step can produce two different next images. One shows the state immediately after the action, including a terminal state. After a reset, a second image shows the new initial state that the policy will use on its next physical step.

```text
s_t / history_t → action_t → physics step → s_terminal_or_next
                                           ├─ save the physical transition for supervision
                                           └─ if done, reset → policy observation for the new episode
```

Replay's `next_state` and `next_depth_stack` must contain the successor the action actually produced. Using a post-reset standing image as the label for a fall would teach the world model that a fall teleports the robot to a standing pose. In the live policy history, fill the reset rows with the new initial state to keep depth frames from the previous episode out of the next one.

`terminated` denotes physical failure and `timeout` denotes truncation at a time or spatial limit. Both delimit data sequences. The task separately defines how death affects the reward and bootstrap. Valid-window checks reject samples spanning episodes and isolate transitions with nonfinite data. Do not train on states invented by `nan_to_num`. States imagined by the actor never enter physical replay.

Commands are time-indexed as well. The action uses the current command, the supervised successor retains its associated command and context, and the next policy observation uses the updated command. The proprioceptive and AMP histories each concatenate by observation term. Their dimensions differ, so flattening both with a generic operation can change the feature order. The v3 discriminator uses post-step policy observations and histories filled in after reset. The world model retains pre-reset physical successors. Section 7.2 describes both contracts.

### 12.3 Replay capacity and precision

With `replay_steps=1000`, replay holds 1,000 vector control steps, each with 4,096 environments. The shared layout stores a physical proprioceptive frame once across overlapping eight-frame histories and shares context across intervals where it stays stable. Exceptions preserve the actual inputs at resets, discontinuities, or other violations of the sharing assumptions.

Sharing preserves the original proprioceptive and context values. Preprocessed visual frames are depths in `[0,1]`, stored as uint8 and converted to floating point by dividing by 255 when sampled. Rounding produces a maximum depth error of about `2.5/(2*255)=0.004902 m`. Single-frame proprioception and context sharing is lossless. Image quantization prevents bitwise recovery of the original floating-point images.

The historical README's fixed-storage estimate of approximately 7.39 GiB used the former 100-dimensional context layout. V2 added 33 material dimensions. V3 uses 29 collision geoms and a 129-dimensional context. The fixed-storage figure excludes models, gradients, optimizer state, graph capture, temporary sampling batches, Warp allocations, and driver memory. Measure peak GPU-process memory on the target training machine.

### 12.4 Reproducing CUDA Graph execution

CUDA Graphs require fixed shapes and long-lived input, parameter, and statistics buffers. With `graph_warmup=3`, three real macro-updates count toward training. Capture performs no extra update. Copy new inputs into existing buffers and retain the same tensor objects after capture. Updating normalization statistics must preserve buffer addresses. Optimizer save/load must restore the state of the same algorithm.

`graph_warmup=3` prepares graph capture. It adds no 500-iteration world-model-only training phase. The current reference schedule uses `model_warmup_iterations=critic_warmup_iterations=0` and H32 throughout imagination. It does not shorten the horizon based on image RMSE, roll back updates for action drift, or veto updates at an error threshold. The v3 default `validation_env_fraction=0` disables independent holdout validation. The JSON field `validation_horizon=32` only specifies a horizon and does not establish that H32 passed validation.

Rounding can vary with CPU execution, TF32, GEMM tiling, and GPU model. AMP uses execution microbatches of 512, accumulates weighted gradients across one logical minibatch, then takes a single AdamW step. Stepping once per execution microbatch would change the update budget. Checkpoint counters and budgets use logical updates.

### 12.5 Execution optimizations and gradient constraints

Current optimizations include packing persistent graph inputs directly, direct replay indexing when all samples are valid, sharing history metadata between current and successor images, deduplicating single-frame histories, capturing fixed-camera acquisition, and reusing H32 kinematics and critic features. The logical workloads remain WM 10 × B2048/K7, actor B4096/H32, and AMP 5 × 4.

Shared FK must reuse the original tensor's computation graph without detaching it. Intermediate features saved for critic regression stay detached, and the terminal bootstrap uses live features. Replay can skip masking and padding only when sample validity has been established. The fallback retains the original rules. Direct indexing preserves the sampling distribution and RNG call conventions. Camera capture must prevent GUI redraws from appending to history and keep reset images out of the world model's pre-reset terminal targets.

Rebuild runtime caches and CUDA Graphs after loading a checkpoint. Keep streams, pools, and persistent-buffer addresses stable. Write directly into captured inputs to avoid stacking and then copying. Do not cache latents from an older encoder to use as new targets. The speed measurements apply to the specific test fixtures. Full v3 training and speedups on another A800 require separate measurements.

### 12.6 Height-field compatibility patch and simulation capacity

The project pins `mujoco-warp==3.8.1`. Its height-field candidate cache can count non-contact triangular prisms toward its 50-entry limit, causing spurious overflow warnings and dropping subsequent contacts. The included script backports the upstream fix and preserves the 3.8.1 `dist < margin` contact convention. Copying the newer `margin+gap` condition directly would change that convention.

```bash
python scripts/fix_mujoco_warp_hfield.py --check --diff
python scripts/fix_mujoco_warp_hfield.py --apply
python scripts/fix_mujoco_warp_hfield.py --check
```

The audited training environment still had the original dependency, with check status `needs_patch`. The default installer performs the check only to reproduce that environment. To test the upstream fix, use the three commands above or pass `--apply-hfield-fix` at installation. Record the resulting dependency change as a separate physics configuration. The script checks the version and SHA256, backs up the original, and rejects unrecognized source. Apply it before starting training because a running Python process and loaded Warp kernels do not automatically reload it. The patch preserves the actual 50-candidate limit and warnings for genuine overflows.

The current task sets `nconmax=256`, `njmax=700`, `ccd_iterations=128`, and `contact_sensor_maxmatch=128`. The total contact pool represented by `nconmax`, per-world constraint capacity, sensor match capacity, and the height field's limit of 50 candidates per geom pair apply at different levels. Increasing one capacity need not fix another. The measurement of at least 172 host contacts came from an older robot scene and does not establish minimum capacity for the v3 assets. Reproduce the configured value of 256. Geom and body counts alone do not determine the contact-pool requirement.

The task retains the 5 cm terrain grid. MuJoCo height fields and PhysX steep-slope triangle meshes still handle slopes differently. Run the separate calibration probe with:

```bash
python scripts/measure_perceptive_sim_capacity.py \
  --num-envs 2 --steps 2 --candidate 256:700:128:128 \
  --output logs/calibration/repro_capacity_probe
```

Use a new output directory. The probe measures physics and capacity and excludes peak memory for the full learner. A two-step run without an error covers only those steps. Other terrains, fallen poses, and the full training run require additional checks.


## 13. Training from scratch, the two clocks, resuming, and independent evaluation

### 13.1 Activate the environment and check the defaults

After installing the isolated environment in Appendix A, run these checks in the newly restored directory.

```bash
source reproduce/activate.sh
python - <<'PY'
from dataclasses import asdict
from scripts.train_wmac_perceptive import parse_config
import json, torch, src.wmac_perceptive, rsl_rl
cfg = parse_config([])
print(json.dumps(asdict(cfg), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
assert cfg.hiking_training_version == 3
assert cfg.sensor_protocol == 'g1_hiking_calibrated_v1'
assert cfg.walking_expert_source == 'pre_hiking_local_walk_turn_v2'
assert cfg.standing_expert_source == 'none'
assert cfg.visual_mode == 'instinct_latent_v1'
assert cfg.locomotion_objective == 'hiking_full_v1'
assert cfg.actor_type == 'moe'
assert cfg.action_limit is None and cfg.validation_env_fraction == 0
assert cfg.wm_window == 7 and cfg.imagination_horizon == 32
assert cfg.iterations == 1_000_000
assert cfg.execution_optimizer == 'muon_adam'
assert torch.cuda.is_available()
print(src.wmac_perceptive.__file__)
print(rsl_rl.__file__)
PY
```

Both source paths must lie under the new directory. The upstream pip distribution `rsl-rl-lib==5.0.1` satisfies mjlab's declared dependency. At runtime, the project root takes precedence on `PYTHONPATH` so Python imports the local AMP fork. Running `pip install -e rsl_rl` would override the package metadata.

### 13.2 Run the 200-control-step GPU integration check first

This check reduces the number of environments, world-model size, and batch sizes. It retains the v3 physics assets, the 129-dimensional context, eight 18 × 32 visual frames, the full reward, and H32. `--iterations 200` advances the vector control clock by 200 steps. Learner updates have their own clock.

```bash
python scripts/train_wmac_perceptive.py \
  --execution-profile supermimic \
  --num-envs 16 --iterations 200 \
  --model-hidden 128 128 \
  --wm-batch-size 32 --wm-updates 1 \
  --actor-batch-size 16 --replay-steps 80 \
  --latent-recon-images 16 \
  --collect-steps 8 --log-interval 1 --save-interval 5 \
  --no-compile --no-cuda-graphs \
  --run-name repro_v3_gpu_smoke
```

Explicitly setting `collect_steps=8` updates the learner roughly once per eight control steps, exercising several cycles of real collection, model fitting, and actor/critic updates. This closed-loop check differs from the full configuration's UTD of 0.4. At 200 control steps it has collected 200 × 16 = 3,200 physical transitions. A CPU scheduling check with the actual `reference_loop` produced 24 learner updates (24 world-model, 24 actor, and 480 critic updates for this configuration), ending at `model_24.pt`. With all samples valid, AMP completes eight blocks, 160 logical discriminator updates, 3,072 policy windows, and 15,360 exposures, with the final eight vector steps pending. If samples are invalid, use the measured valid counts.

To check compilation and CUDA Graphs, remove both `--no-...` flags, choose a new run name, and add `--discriminator-batch-size 32`. At N16 the full logical AMP batch has 96 samples, divisible by 32, so the test can exercise AMP capture. Invalid samples can cause an individual update to fall back. The default of 512 processes only 96 samples at N16 and does not guarantee AMP graph capture.

`runtime.json` is written on completion or failure. During training, follow the console and `metrics.csv`. Check that model, actor, and critic updates execute, AMP completes blocks and exposures, measured gradients are finite and nonzero, and the physical simulation advances. With no v3 holdout, `validation_model_error=NaN` is expected. Some legacy diagnostics also use NaN when inapplicable, so individual CSV columns can legitimately contain it.

### 13.3 Full training from scratch and the optional Transformer comparison

```bash
python scripts/train_wmac_perceptive.py \
  --execution-profile supermimic \
  --num-envs 4096 --seed 42 \
  --iterations 1000000 \
  --run-name hiking_v3_from_zero
```

This command starts without an existing model, private checkpoint, or warm-start parameters. The default output is `logs/wmac_perceptive/<timestamp>_seed42_hiking_v3_from_zero/`. One million vector control steps ideally produce approximately 4.096 billion physical transitions across individual environments. The optimizer has a separate counter, and the sufficiency of this budget for convergence has yet to be established.

Run the optional attention actor as a separate experiment.

```bash
python scripts/train_wmac_perceptive.py \
  --actor-type transformer \
  --num-envs 4096 --seed 42 --iterations 1000000 \
  --run-name hiking_v3_transformer_from_zero
```

The two actors use different architectures and optimizer parameter groups. Record their results separately. Ordinary resume cannot switch between them.

| Setting | Current full-training default |
| --- | --- |
| Parallel environments / control dt / decimation | 4096 / 0.02 s / 4 |
| World model | 2048 × 3, GELU + LayerNorm. Ten updates per learner update, B2048, seven transitions. |
| Replay | 1,000 vector time steps, shared uint8 frames on GPU, 129-dimensional context |
| Actor | B4096, H32, one update per learner update. The default four-expert MoE uses a linear gate. |
| Critic | Input dimension 281, hidden widths 256/128, five epochs × four minibatches, gamma .99, lambda .95 |
| World-model / actor / critic learning rates | All constant at 2e-4. Chapter 9 gives the Muon/Adam parameter partition. |
| AMP | One block per 24 fresh vector steps, five epochs × four logical minibatches, AdamW with learning rate 1e-4 |
| Exploration / raw action clipping | Gaussian standard deviation .1. `action_limit=None` leaves raw actions unclipped. |
| First trainable replay window | At least eight frames. Initial filling counts toward the vector-step budget. |
| Control-step-to-learner schedule | `collect_steps=0`, UTD=.4, Ratio accumulator |
| TF32 / compile / CUDA Graph | True / True / True |
| Logging / saving intervals | Every 50 / 1,000 learner updates |
| Holdout / automatic physical evaluation | Split 0, no independent holdout. Separate scripts perform physical evaluation. |

`reproduce/verify-offline-inputs.py` writes the complete configuration to `reproduce/reference-config.json`. Each training run records the effective settings after CLI overrides in its `config.json`.

### 13.4 Three counters and checkpoint names

```text
vector_step = number of completed parallel control steps, each advancing all N environments once
sim_steps = N * vector_step
iteration = number of completed learner macro-updates
Per learner macro-update: 10 WM optimizer updates + 1 actor update + 20 critic minibatch updates
AMP runs independently every 24 fresh vector steps, without resampling once per learner iteration.
```

With the default Ratio of .4 and K=7, the first eight control steps build usable replay. The first learner update occurs at `vector_step=9`, followed by 11, 14, 16, 19, and so on. Ratio events with insufficient history are skipped. There is no separate eight-step precollection phase. An explicit `--collect-steps` override sets Ratio to `1/collect_steps`.

In `model_<iteration>.pt`, the number counts learner updates and matches the console's `iter`. The same unit applies to `--save-interval`. The first control step can write `model_0.pt`, and the final control step also saves the current iteration. Read the protocol in older `model_step_<control_step>.pt` checkpoints to interpret their counters, since the name alone is insufficient.

V3 leaves a final partial AMP block pending when it contains fewer than 24 fresh steps. Use the number of completed blocks to count blocks and exposures in short runs. The earlier convention of always flushing the tail at termination does not apply. For the default one million control steps and no invalid samples, the number of complete blocks is `floor(1000000/24)`, each with 20 discriminator updates.

### 13.5 Locate the latest checkpoint and resume

Find the highest-numbered checkpoint for the latest full MoE run on the local machine.

```bash
export AMP_REPRO_CKPT="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
runs = sorted(Path('logs/wmac_perceptive').glob('*_hiking_v3_from_zero'))
if not runs:
    raise SystemExit('No hiking_v3_from_zero run directory found')
paths = [p for p in runs[-1].glob('model_*.pt') if re.fullmatch(r'model_[0-9]+', p.stem)]
if not paths:
    raise SystemExit('The selected run has no checkpoints yet')
print(max(paths, key=lambda p: int(p.stem.split('_')[-1])).resolve())
PY
)"
test -f "$AMP_REPRO_CKPT"
```

For example, extend the total vector-step budget to 1.2 million.

```bash
python scripts/train_wmac_perceptive.py \
  --resume "$AMP_REPRO_CKPT" \
  --iterations 1200000 --run-name hiking_v3_resumed
```

The 1.2 million steps are the total through the end of training. Resume restores the actor, robot, sensor, motion pool, versions, and optimizer configuration from the checkpoint. Ordinary resume requires the original protocols. The v1 full context of 100, the v2 context of 133 with the older physics model, and the v3 context of 129 with the new input normalization are not directly compatible.

Replay and live simulation state are omitted from checkpoints. Resume must collect history again. It restores networks, optimizers, `sim_steps`, `iteration`, and the Ratio accumulator. Refilling replay can skip some learner events, so bitwise continuation of the trajectory is not guaranteed. Changing a version number in JSON cannot migrate the checkpoint.

### 13.6 Interactive playback, quantitative evaluation, and starts from rest

```bash
python scripts/evaluate_wmac_perceptive.py \
  --checkpoint "$AMP_REPRO_CKPT" \
  --device cuda:0 --mode walk \
  --num-envs 128 --steps 500 --seed 2032 --save-trace

python scripts/evaluate_wmac_zero_start.py \
  --checkpoint "$AMP_REPRO_CKPT" \
  --device cuda:0 --num-envs 32 --seeds 2032 2033 \
  --cases stand start immediate_start \
  --terrain flat --domain-randomization retained

python scripts/play_wmac_perceptive.py \
  --checkpoint "$AMP_REPRO_CKPT" \
  --device cuda:0 --mode walk --viewer viser
```

Interactive playback in v3 defaults to ten environments, 10 s episodes, and a 4 × 10 terrain grid without walls. It retains proprioceptive noise and the curriculum, removes startup material randomization and low-height failure, and sets joint reset perturbations to zero while retaining root-velocity perturbations. Quantitative evaluation additionally disables all observation noise. Its results apply to those specific PLAY conditions. The 20 s training environment has a different terrain and termination distribution. The zero-start evaluation also resets flat terrain, commands, initial velocities, and history. Selecting `retained` does not reinstate material events already removed by PLAY. See Chapter 11 for the full settings.

The default browser address is `http://127.0.0.1:8081`. Use `--viewer native` for a desktop window or `--viewer none --steps 500` for a headless smoke test. Resume and evaluation build the actor from the saved architecture, including the Transformer variant. During inference each next image comes from the simulator, without substitution by the world model.

Report first-episode survival, timeouts, velocity and lateral errors, progress toward the target, and drift at zero commanded speed. Include seeds, sample denominators, and PLAY conditions. Distinguish timeouts from falls and report command tracking and standing still separately from fall avoidance.

### 13.7 Monitoring, read-only analysis, and profiling

```bash
tensorboard --logdir logs/wmac_perceptive --port 6006
python scripts/analyze_wmac_perceptive_speed.py --help
```

The analysis script reads the existing CSV, configuration, and runtime files. It reports time by phase using elapsed wall time and physical and imagined step counts. Host-side time fractions do not measure GPU utilization. For a new profile, the following command starts a normal training run and writes a trace as a separate diagnostic experiment.

```bash
python scripts/profile_wmac_perceptive.py \
  --profile-wait-iterations 100 --profile-active-iterations 24 \
  -- --num-envs 4096 --iterations 1000000 --run-name hiking_v3_profile
```

The profiler times complete learner macro-updates, one per `_log` call. By default it waits for 100, warms up for one, and records 24 active updates. Normal training continues after this single window. These window counts use learner updates, while the main CLI budget uses vector control steps.

Inspect the physical rewards and terminations, multistep world-model error, 13 auxiliary heads, latent/persistence/reconstruction metrics, actual actor gradients, AMP blocks/windows/exposures, and whether graph capture actually ran. With a zero holdout fraction, low training loss does not establish generalization. Small latent MSE does not guarantee correct directional derivatives with respect to actions. Assess control using both checkpoints and physical evaluation results.


## 14. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Action |
| --- | --- |
| SHA256 mismatch or missing block during restoration | Download a complete Markdown file again. Keep the checksum verification and replace missing data from the intact file. |
| Missing shared drive or old host directory | The restored project is independent of those paths. Check for an old `activate_env.sh` or symlinks copied from the original machine. Use `source reproduce/activate.sh`. |
| Python imports pip's `rsl_rl` | The shell's `PYTHONPATH` lacks the restored root. Reactivate the isolated environment and inspect `rsl_rl.__file__`. |
| Unrecognized `history_ordering` | The observation-manager patch is missing from mjlab in the active interpreter. Repeat that installer step and check which interpreter it uses. |
| Height-field patch rejects the SHA | Reinstall the pinned dependency in the isolated environment to get a recognized original or patched version. Run `--check --diff` first and keep the checksum checks. |
| Repeated `height field collision overflow` | Check that the upstream fix was actually loaded and distinguish false warnings from genuine 50-candidate overflow. Record results with the separate capacity probe. Disabling logs only hides the warning. |
| GPU out of memory | Start with the small-scale command. Reducing N, batch size, replay size, or network size changes the full-training conditions. Document the overrides, including any change from H32 to H8. |
| Graph capture or compilation problem | Check eager mode with the same task and H32 using `--no-compile --no-cuda-graphs`. Then enable compilation and graph capture separately to isolate the difference. |
| Model learns but AMP updates stay at zero | Check whether 24 fresh vector steps accumulated and whether episode boundaries or nonfinite values invalidated windows. Inspect the current AMP log rather than the historical 2 × 512 fields. |
| Dimension mismatch when loading an earlier model | Check v1/v2/v3, contexts 100/133/129, critic input 315/281, new 97-dimensional WM normalization, actor type, and camera protocol. Start a separate experiment when changing protocols. |
| No GPU or `torch.cuda.is_available()` is False | Fix the driver, device visibility, and CUDA wheels first. CPU tests can run separately and cover only the CPU paths. |
| Equations fail to render in Feishu | The equations use plain text and require no plugin. Retain the fenced equation blocks when copying, including the full expressions. |

## 15. Verification results and limits of the method

### 15.1 Checks repeated when this handbook was written

This revision updated the documentation and reproduction artifacts. It left the existing algorithms, rewards, task configurations, active training processes, and model weights in their original state. Appendix A.7 records the tests, data-pool checks, and restoration from the final Markdown performed for that revision. Historical test counts belong to their respective runs.

The following existing tests can be audited individually.

| Test | What it checks |
| --- | --- |
| `test_reference_visual_gradients.py` | Against pinned upstream code: actor visual detach, gradients from the latent to later physical states, reconstruction as the sole source of encoder gradients, and terminal value gradients with respect to its inputs |
| `test_hiking_training_v2.py`, `test_hiking_reference_robot.py` | Coupled settings for v2 compatibility, and the v3 physics assets, inputs, FK, and protocols |
| `test_hiking_soft_termination.py` | The v2/v3 forward probability and its derivative come from the same smooth function |
| `test_wm_continuous_normalization.py` | V2 continues updating statistics beyond 2e8 |
| `test_hiking_amp_budget.py`, `test_hiking_amp_logical_execution.py` | The 24-step cursor, complete sample reuse, and gradient weighting across logical minibatches and execution microbatches |
| `test_hiking_full_rewards.py`, `test_hiking_full_world_model.py` | Agreement between physical and imagined computation for the 26 formulas with actual labels injected |
| `test_perceptive_capture_layout.py`, `test_deduplicated_replay.py` | Capture buffers, resets, episode boundaries, and reconstruction of shared history |

Some upstream comparisons require optional checkouts at pinned revisions and skip when these are unavailable. The appendix gives download commands. Report passed, skipped, and failed tests separately. A successful command exit code does not establish that all optional comparisons ran.

### 15.2 Equivalence claims that remain unverified

MuJoCo and PhysX differ in collision handling, joint solvers, height fields, static/dynamic friction, and restitution interfaces. The world model is conditioned on the actual sliding friction. The source samples of static friction and restitution are retained for audit, without inventing an uncalibrated `solref` mapping. V3 ports the official URDF inertias, collision geometry, and joints. The local model uses a pelvis root and the source uses a torso root. Asset adaptation leaves engine-specific solver and contact differences.

Physical supervision of auxiliary heads does not establish the accuracy of their imagined gradients. Depth reconstruction does not establish that the latent represents all information relevant to action. Stop-gradient preserves a specific upstream training boundary, whose optimality for this task remains untested. The camera measurements establish acquisition at approximately 30 Hz. They do not measure the full latency from exposure to policy consumption. A 50 Hz simulated observation rate does not establish that a real robot can supply a fresh image at 50 Hz.

This handbook establishes the feasibility of restoring the complete code and data and checking the environment and training paths step by step. Full-training performance under the new protocol, large-scale traversal success across terrains, physical robot performance, and speedup over the original PPO all require measurement under fixed evaluation protocols. The original SuperMimic and Hiking papers report their own results.

- Motion priors and adversarial style rewards. [AMP paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.02180)
- Background on world models and BPTT. Chapter 2 identifies the exact engineering revisions used here. [SuperMimic project](https://supermimic.github.io/) and [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480)
- The implementation used as the source for the visual latent and stop-gradient. [Pinned InstinctMJ Parkour source](https://github.com/project-instinct/InstinctMJ/blob/03563ee02665f327425106372264070315673748/src/instinct_mj/rl/supermimic/parkour/runner.py)
- The task, depth policy, and safe foothold design. [Hiking project](https://project-instinct.github.io/hiking-in-the-wild/) and [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.07718)
